svg.title: A timer on a ticket: start, stop, and the worklog writes itself — SoftTrack web design mockup (#266)
svg.desc: Time is logged after the fact, which is why time logged at the end of the week is a guess. Starting a timer on a ticket shows it in the header on every page; stopping opens the log-time form with the minutes filled in; there is one timer per person; and a timer left running asks what it should have been.
svg.text: A timer on a ticket: start, stop, and the worklog writes itself

svg.text: Done when a timer can be started on a ticket and shows in the header on every page, stopping opens the log-time form filled in with the minutes and today’s date, starting a
second timer stops the first and offers to log it, the start time is kept on the server, a timer running for more than ten hours asks what it should have been and never logs by itself,

g.text: In the header on every page
the ticket’s key and the time so far.
One click stops it from anywhere.
The start time is kept on the server.
The timer survives a closed tab
and is the same timer on a phone.
It never logs by itself. After ten hours it asks, and the answer is
